title: Is Dropshipping Worth It in 2026? (An Honest Assessment) | Side Hustle School
summary: Honest assessment of dropshipping: thin margins, ad costs, supplier problems, and saturation sink most beginners, while niche stores and adjacent models can work.

assertions.quote: that version doesn't work for the vast majority of people who try it
you can easily spend more on ads than you make in profit
Customers blame you—because they bought from your store, not from some warehouse overseas.
The most commonly dropshipped products—phone cases, fitness accessories, pet gadgets—are sold by thousands of nearly identical stores.
someone finds a specific audience with an underserved need, then builds a store around solving that problem
What dropshipping isn't: a business strategy. It's just a way of handling shipping and inventory.
treat it like an actual business rather than a passive income hack
If Etsy changes its algorithm or Amazon suspends your listing, you can lose your revenue overnight.

verdicts.note: Platform-dependency risk is widely documented among marketplace sellers.

Amazon suspended the majority of Empire-managed stores within months; a suspension locked any earnings the store had generated and appeals took months, leaving clients with credit-card debt they could not repay from sales.

assertions.quote: No shipping, no suppliers, no inventory, near-100% margins.

verdicts.note: Marginal cost is near zero; the cost shifts to creation and marketing.

assertions.quote: Most brand-new Shopify stores sit at zero visitors until the owner actively promotes them.

verdicts.note: A standalone domain has no organic discovery; traffic must be bought or earned.
